changes.why: The CHK-003 helper model counted only PutFullData full-word writes to ALERT_TEST as fatal_fault/regwen writes. The specification does not limit the opcode, and a full-word PutPartialData (a_size=2, mask 1111) is a legal 4-byte write that succeeds. So a write of 1 to fatal_fault made with PutPartialData while regwen=1 must count as a qualifying write. wr0_w now accepts opcode 0 or 1, and qual_w and p_clr follow from it. The assertion, the count bound and the 16-cycle bound are unchanged.

The CHK-004 IE_0 model updated ie on a byte write (a_size 0, mask 0001) to INTR_ENABLE0 only when the opcode was PutPartialData. D-013 does not restrict the opcode: such a byte write "has the effect of the write". So an error-free PutFullData byte write that sets IE_0=1 left the model at ie=0, and the assertion wrongly required o_intr_timer_expired=0. The byte-write term now uses is_wr (PutFullData or PutPartialData). The update still happens only on a D beat with d_error=0. The assertion itself is unchanged.

notes:
I fixed both faults with changes to the SVA checkers only. Nothing was simulated or proven formally, so both checks need to be rerun.

Fault 1 (nnc_chk_alert.sv): a full-word write to ALERT_TEST now counts whether it is PutFullData or PutPartialData. The CHK-003 assertion and its bounds are unchanged.

Fault 2 (nnc_chk_intr.sv): the INTR_ENABLE0 model now also updates on a PutFullData byte write. The CHK-004 assertion is unchanged.

Out of scope for me (TASK.md only allows edits to verif/sva/*.sv and verif/tests/*.py, excluding nnc_cocotb.py, and nnc_env.sv is read only):
1) contract.json still describes the old behaviour. The CHK-003 text at line 302 (both the regwen model and the qualifying write) should read "a PutFullData or PutPartialData with a_size=2 and mask 1111". The CHK-004 text at line 316 should read "a PutFullData/PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001". The checkers now differ from the contract wording until it is updated.
2) Fault 2 also suggests adding the D-016 assumption (i_a_valid=0 during reset and in the first cycle after release) to verif/formal/nnc_env.sv. That file is read only, so this is left to the environment owner. It is not needed for the CHK-004 fix.
3) Fault 2 suggests the same review for CHK-011. Its d_error=0 list in nnc_chk_tlul.sv (noerr_req, line 109) and expected_error() in test_ot_rv_timer.py still name only PutPartialData for byte writes. I left them alone to keep the change minimal. Widening them would add a new d_error=0 requirement on PutFullData byte writes: D-013 supports it, but contract.json line 1272 says the D-013 byte writes are issued as PutPartialData. The checker designer should decide on that separately.
